title: From Copilots to Agents: Rebuilding the Company Around AI
thesis: This episode argues that Kavak successfully rebuilt its company around AI agents, transitioning from a traditional marketplace to an automated platform that handles over 90% of customer interactions. The core thesis is that this 'streaming transition'—compared to Netflix's move to streaming—was essential for survival and growth, allowing the business to scale its infrastructure four times beyond its previous state despite a period of flat growth and market implosion.

claims.claim: Kavak is an all-in-one marketplace for car-related services in Latin America and the Middle East, managing the user journey from selling to buying a car.
claims.quote: Kavak is an all in one market place to do anything related to your car. We work out of Latin America. We work in Mexico, Brazil, Chile, Argentina. We also have operations in the Middle East.

claims.claim: Kavak manages the end-to-end process of a user's journey while they own their car, including buying, reconditioning, selling, financing, and warranties.
claims.quote: We manage the end-to-end process of a user's journey while they own their car. We do everything. We buy these cars. We recondition them. We then sell them online. We provide the financing to our users as well. We manage their warranties or services throughout the process.

claims.claim: Kavak is the biggest e-commerce auto business in Latin America with around 10,000 transactions every month and 3,500 employees.
claims.quote: In terms of scale, well, the business is probably the biggest e-commerce auto business in Latin America. We do around 10,000 transactions every month growing very fast. We have around 3500 people. Yeah.

claims.claim: Kavak uses AI agents to handle more than 90% of customer interactions after a transition that took a full year of flat growth.
claims.quote: Instead of retreating, Carlos bet on AI replacing co-pilot tools that employees wouldn't adopt with agents that now handle more than 90% of customer interactions. The transition took a full year of flat growth.

claims.claim: Kavak was founded by Carlos Garcia Otati after he was defrauded twice trying to buy and sell cars in the region.
claims.quote: Carlos Garcia Otati founded Kavak after being defrauded twice trying to buy and sell cars in the region. The company he built handles everything, buying, reconditioning, selling, financing, warranties, and logistics.

claims.claim: Kavak operates across Latin America and the Middle East with four separate businesses underneath one consumer experience.
claims.quote: Four separate businesses underneath one consumer experience operating across Latin America and the Middle East. By 2021, Kavak had 10,000 employees and was growing at 300%.
